Create one transparent RGBA landscape sheet, 1536x1024, arranged in EXACTLY three columns and two rows, six isolated connected plant sprites. No text, no borders, no water or scenery behind the objects, no baked glow or drop shadows; true transparent background. Upper middle: one different golden olive kelp stalk, sinuous stem and longer wavy ribbon blades, about 420px tall, 280px wide. Whole subjects fully visible, roots touching their own stone/base, no floor lines, no disconnected particles.
reefs: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent parallax scenery atlas for DeepFeast, a polished side-view 2D underwater fish game. ONE RGBA landscape sheet 1536x1024 with EXACTLY FOUR large separate reef formations in TWO columns and TWO rows. Each formation is one connected object, isolated with clear transparent gutters and a flat grounded base. No scene backdrop, no water, no fish, no light rays, no text, no frames, no cast shadow, true transparent negative space including holes in arches. Top left: a long low reef shelf with several softly rounded limestone boulders, one small rising pillar and a few muted teal coral fans, approximately 640x330px. Top right: a weathered natural coral-rock arch, wide low bridge with an organic oval opening, flanked by stacked rounded reef stones and sparse sea plants, approximately 640x360px. Bottom left: a different wide rocky ridge with tiered rounded plate-coral shelves, some scalloped sea fans and wispy green seaweed, approximately 640x320px. Bottom right: a wide dark abyss basalt outcrop with gently curved eroded stone fingers, small cool violet deep-sea tube sponges and a few tiny dim cyan tips, approximately 640x330px. Do not make buildings or mountains. Art: hand-painted stylized casual-game scenery, softly sculpted volume, tasteful brush texture and broken edges, subtle upper-left light. Restrained underwater palette blue teal slate with pale turquoise highlights in first three formations, deep blue-violet in fourth. Soft contrast, no harsh black outlines; these will appear through water behind brightly colored painted fish and foreground coral. Silhouettes must be natural and rounded, readable as underwater habitats rather than conical mountains. Complete formations fully inside their cells, continuous opaque stone footing at bottom of each object, no detached specks or unattached objects.
